title: Binomial Distribution
subject: Mathematics
subtitle: Class 12 HSC & MHT-CET • Rapid Revision Deck

cards.q: What is a Bernoulli Trial?
cards.a: A random experiment with exactly two mutually exclusive outcomes ('Success' S and 'Failure' F), where trials are independent and probability of success p remains constant throughout.
cards.hint: p + q = 1, where q is the probability of failure.

cards.q: Definition and notation of a Binomial Random Variable?
cards.a: X ~ B(n, p): Represents the number of successes in n independent Bernoulli trials, where n is a fixed positive integer (n ∈ N) and 0 < p < 1.
cards.hint: The parameters of a binomial distribution are n and p.

cards.q: Probability Mass Function (p.m.f.) of X ~ B(n, p)?
cards.a:
P(X = x) = ⁿCₓ · pˣ · qⁿ⁻ˣ, for x = 0, 1, 2, ..., n (and 0 otherwise),
where q = 1 - p.
cards.hint: ⁿCₓ = n! / [ x! (n - x)! ]. Possible values of x start at 0 and go up to n.

cards.q: Formulas for Mean, Variance, and Standard Deviation of X ~ B(n, p)?
cards.a:
Mean: E(X) = μ = n · p
Variance: Var(X) = σ² = n · p · q
Standard Deviation: σ = √(n · p · q).
cards.hint: Since q = 1 - p, Var(X) = n p (1 - p).

cards.q: THE FUNDAMENTAL INEQUALITY: Can Variance be greater than or equal to Mean in Binomial Distribution?
cards.a: NO! In any Binomial Distribution, Var(X) < E(X) ALWAYS (since 0 < q < 1, npq < np).
cards.hint: Top MHT-CET trap: 'Can a binomial distribution have mean = 5 and variance = 6?' Answer is strictly NO!

cards.q: How to find parameters n and p given Mean and Variance?
cards.a:
1. Divide Variance by Mean: q = Var(X) / E(X) = (n p q) / (n p).
2. Find p: p = 1 - q.
3. Find n: n = E(X) / p.
cards.hint: Standard 2-mark question in HSC Board exams and common 10-second CET MCQ.

cards.q: Maximum possible Variance of X ~ B(n, p) for a given n?
cards.a: Maximum variance occurs when p = q = 1/2, giving Var_max(X) = n / 4.
cards.hint: Since p(1 - p) has a maximum value of 1/4 at p = 1/2.

cards.q: Shortcut formula for 'At least one success' P(X ≥ 1)?
cards.hint: Complement rule! Much faster than calculating P(1) + P(2) + ... + P(n).

cards.q: Formula for 'At most one success' P(X ≤ 1)?
cards.hint: Only involves x = 0 and x = 1.

cards.q: Symmetric Binomial Distribution condition?
cards.a: When p = q = 1/2. The distribution is perfectly symmetrical about mean μ = n/2, with ⁿCₓ = ⁿC_{n-x}.
cards.hint: Example: Tossing a fair coin n times.

cards.q: Skewness of Binomial Distribution based on p?
cards.a:
If p < 1/2 (p < q): Positively skewed (skewed to the right).
If p > 1/2 (p > q): Negatively skewed (skewed to the left).
If p = 1/2: Symmetric (zero skewness).
cards.hint: Peak shifts toward the side of the larger probability.

cards.q: How to find the Mode of a Binomial Distribution?
cards.a:
Compute (n + 1) · p:
1. If (n + 1)p is an integer m ⇒ Bimodal, with modes at (m - 1) and m.
2. If (n + 1)p is not an integer ⇒ Unimodal, mode is the integer part [ (n + 1)p ].
cards.hint: The mode is the value of x with the highest probability P(X = x).

cards.q: Recurrence relation between consecutive probabilities P(X = x + 1) and P(X = x)?
cards.hint: Eliminates calculating large factorials for consecutive probabilities.

cards.q: Sum of all probabilities in a Binomial Distribution?
cards.a: ∑_{x=0}^n P(X = x) = ∑_{x=0}^n ⁿCₓ pˣ qⁿ⁻ˣ = (q + p)ⁿ = 1ⁿ = 1.
cards.hint: Direct expansion of the binomial theorem for (q + p)ⁿ.

cards.q: A fair coin is tossed 6 times. Find probability of getting exactly 4 heads.
A die is thrown 5 times. Getting a 5 or 6 is a success. Find Mean and Variance.
cards.hint: Check: Var(X) = 10/9 < 15/9 = Mean (satisfies fundamental inequality).

cards.q: A fair coin is tossed n times. Minimum number of tosses so that probability of at least one head > 0.99?
cards.hint: Since 2⁶ = 64 < 100 and 2⁷ = 128 > 100, minimum tosses n = 7.

cards.q: Binomial Distribution as a sum of Bernoulli random variables?
cards.a: X = X₁ + X₂ + ... + Xₙ, where each Xᵢ is an independent Bernoulli(p) variable taking value 1 (success) or 0 (failure).
cards.hint: E(X) = ∑ E(Xᵢ) = n p; Var(X) = ∑ Var(Xᵢ) = n p q.

cards.q: Mean and Variance of a single Bernoulli trial?
cards.a:
Mean = p
Variance = p · q = p · (1 - p).
cards.hint: Bernoulli trial is simply B(1, p).

cards.q: If X ~ B(n, p) with E(X) = 4 and Var(X) = 3, find P(X = 0).
cards.hint: Quickly determine q, p, n first, then compute P(X = 0) = qⁿ.

cards.q: For X ~ B(n, p), if P(X = 2) = P(X = 3) and n = 5, find p.
cards.a: ⁵C₂ p² q³ = ⁵C₃ p³ q² ⇒ 10 p² q³ = 10 p³ q² ⇒ q = p ⇒ 1 - p = p ⇒ 2p = 1 ⇒ p = 1/2.
cards.hint: ⁵C₂ = ⁵C₃ = 10, so powers of p and q equate to give p = q.

cards.q: MCQ exam guessing model: 10 questions, each with 4 choices. What is expected score?
cards.a:
n = 10, p = 1/4 (chance of guessing correctly).
Expected score E(X) = n p = 10 × (1/4) = 2.5 correct answers.

cards.q: MHT-CET calculation saver: Finding P(X ≥ 2)?
cards.hint: Never add P(2) + P(3) + ... + P(n); always subtract the complementary 0 and 1 cases from 1.

cards.q: Ratio of P(X = x) to P(X = x - 1) in B(n, p)?
cards.hint: Helpful to find which term in the distribution is the maximum (mode).

cards.q: If X ~ B(n, p) has Mean = 2 and SD = 1, what are n and p?
cards.hint: Distribution is X ~ B(4, 1/2).
